coverage.target: NFR1 (feed content displays within 2 seconds) is specifically FeedUnit's own listPosts request-path target (feed-unit's NFR1.1); this Unit's analogous concern is its own client-side cold-start/transition targets (NFR-PERF.1, NFR-PERF.2), which are Unit-local, not a claim of NFR1 coverage

NFR2 (best-effort availability) is a backend-service concern; scalability/reliability/observability-requirements.md do not apply to this kind: ui Unit per the stage's produces_kinds rule — this Unit has no server-side availability of its own to target
NFR3 (payment-data handling) belongs to donation-unit; this Unit never handles raw payment details, per functional-spec.md's Donate workflow explicitly deferring to the aggregator's own checkout UI
NFR4.1 (data protection — credential storage, transport encryption)
NFR5 (payment reconciliation) belongs to donation-unit; this Unit only displays Donation status, never resolves it (functional-spec.md's own explicit statement)
NFR6.1 (services/-layer access boundary and mandatory self-review before merging service-layer or access-gating changes)

Accessibility (WCAG AA baseline, requirements.md's own stated target) is this Unit's own concern — it owns every screen's rendering. No separate NFR7.x elaboration is added at this stage beyond restating that the baseline (already confirmed at Rough Mockups, Q4) applies to every screen this Unit builds; this stage found no additional accessibility target to quantify beyond the existing WCAG AA baseline
Testing methodology/coverage floor is a cross-cutting Build and Test concern, not a Unit-level NFR target

note: performance-requirements.md (NFR-PERF.1-3) and security-requirements.md's NFR-AUTHZ.2/NFR-CRASH.1 are intentionally outside the NFR1-NFR8 inheritance chain above: inception's requirements.md defines no client-startup-performance or crash-reporting NFR, so these use Unit-local IDs rather than a fabricated inception sub-ID. This is the only Unit in the project for which scalability-requirements.md, reliability-requirements.md, and observability-requirements.md are not produced at all (kind: ui, per the stage's produces_kinds rule) — NFR2's availability concern and any observability need are therefore marked N/A/absorbed into security-requirements.md's NFR-CRASH.1 rather than given their own file.
